title: PRESSER | Pete Golding - MSU Postgame (11-27-26)
text: Yeah. No. Uh just really proud of the effort that we came out with in the second half. You know, obviously the first half uh wasn't what we envisioned. Uh I thought we couldn't really get in rhythm on offense. Uh didn't do a really good job, you know, spreading the ball around. Had some drops. You know, I thought defensively gave up the explosive play. Um and then penalties uh were really hurting us, but really challenged them at halftime. Um I thought they came out, you know, 35 to7 in the second half. You know, in that rivalry, uh I thought a lot of players stepped up. I thought Josh Dy really stepped up in the second half. Uh the competitive character of Trinidad, some guys made some big plays. Thought Blake Purchase played really well. Um and Big Will, I think, had a really big night. So was was really proud of how they responded in the second half. Um they knew what this game meant, you know, not only to our locker room, but to our school and to our town, to our former alumni. I thought Tom Luke did an unbelievable job on Sunday, you know, making sure those 51 new guys uh knew what this rivalry actually meant. And I think that's the benefit of, you know, having 18 guys in the building that have played in this game that are now on staff. Uh I think our team felt that, you know, this week and and came out in the second half and responded. Uh so it's always great to win regardless. I think it's always really good to beat a rival a rivalry, especially, you know, the last regular season game. I think it gives us a little momentum uh moving into the bowl game. So I was really proud of their effort. Raise your hands question. >> Pet know Trinidad already said that he's going to be playing uh in the bowl game, but this was obviously his his last home start. Um I guess just kind of broadly how how do you think his miss career should be remembered by fans? >> Yeah, I mean I think that's up to the to the miss fans, you know, to to me explosive. You know, when I think about Trinidad, uh I think it's breathtaking moments, you know, you think you got them sacked and you don't. the ability to extend plays and and make a lot of plays. Like when I think about Trinidad, I think about that smile. Uh I think he's got a contagious personality. Um when I think about him, I think about what type of dude he is and what a good teammate he is and what he's done, you know, not only for this school, but for this town. Um but, you know, from a quarterback standpoint, I think you think about he's a winner. I mean, he's got an elite competitive character. And uh you know, I know this didn't go exactly how he saw fit and a lot of people didn't, but he kept his head down and competed his butt off. uh was a really good teammate and and I think it goes to show you even before this game that there was no decision for him whether he was going to be with his team and play for this school and a school in a town that's done so much for him and that's not common now unfortunately you know so I think it goes to show who he is and how he's wired and what this place has done for him. >> I know you're fresh off the field but just how would you kind of evaluate the job you've done as a head coach in your first season? >> I think plenty of y'all will evaluate that for me. Uh but uh no obviously, man, I'm a competitor and and always have been. So, you know, we're going to find, you know, the best way to do things and you go back and you open the book up, you know, and I don't have regrets of how it was done in the offseason or any of that. I I don't look at it that way. I I look at where we're at right now and what we need to do moving forward to play championship football. And that's looking at the roster. That's looking at the staff. That's looking at my job description. So, and that's going to be every year. That's no different. How wouldn't it different than, you know, evaluation of last year? You know, I think sometimes it's harder coming off successful seasons, right? To really look in the mirror and make sure you're still changing and and doing the things necessary. You know, that this one's going to be pretty easy for me to be honest with you. >> Uh, real quick, what did you think of Will's dog pee celebration? And and maybe more broadly, what what is he meant to >> Hold on. Say that first part again. >> Did you see it? I don't know if you saw Will did the the piss and miss celebration. Okay. >> So, what did he do? He did the the piss and miss. >> Of course he did. That's great. >> Well, so maybe >> real classy. Yeah. >> Well, maybe what what does a guy like that meant to this program and and you know in the Egg Bowl rivalry for you guys? >> You know, I mean Cam and Will have a special place in my heart based on when I first got here. You know, I thought one of the most important things was kind of, you know, changing the pattern of elite D linemen in this state, having the ability to come in here and be good on defense and compete at a high level and compete for championships and be first round draft picks. And so, you know, in 23 when I came in that January of 23, those were the two guys that we really focused on early like, man, we've got to get these two guys to change the narrative. And those two at that point, you know, that was coming off of a year they lost the last five games of the year. you know, it wasn't in the same position, you know, that it was, you know, these last couple years. So, those dudes took a step of faith, you know, to be honest with you, that, hey, you know, the defense is going to show versatility for them and we're going to play at a championship level, um, on top of improving their draft status. And so, you know, Will for me was kind of that first project to where, hey, this is what the three-year plan looks like. And his mom and I were talking last week, she's like, coach, like, I can bring out that piece of paper right now. remember that meeting and what exactly that we talked about and then now to see it come to fruition. So, it doesn't always work out that way. Uh but for him to take that step, uh what he's meant for our locker room, how he goes about his business, uh he's a professional, he practices butt off, he competes his butt off, uh and he loves his school and he loves this town. So, a dude from Houston, Mississippi that, you know, that hadn't been the norm in the past. So, uh just really appreciate him and how he's handled himself and he's a heck of a player, no doubt. He's got a really bright future, but he's unbelievable dude. >> Do you think that was it for Will? >> You know, uh, no. I I don't think so. Um, I'm not going to speak, you know, obviously, you know, we've had retention meetings and all that, you know, and I told him, I speak to him like my own son, you know, I was like, you know, my job was for you to come in here and develop as a player and as a man and have unbelievable experience. Um, make a new circle for yourself for the next 40 to 50 years of your life. Uh, and his goal has always been a first round draft pick. you know, that that's what he wanted out of college football. You know, that's the first thing I always ask those guys like, look, what are you looking for out of college football? Not school, just college football. He's like, "Coach, I want to be a first round draft pick." And so, you know, they're going through the information stage of all that. And I told his mom and I told him, I said, "Look, man, if you're a top 20 draft pick, I'm not asking you to come back. That that's bad business. You know, that that's been your goal. That's your aspirations and uh that's significant. So, uh you know, we're going to continue to get the information and give it to his family. you know, it's a family decision for him, but uh I I I would be shocked if he doesn't participate in the bowl game regardless. >> Questions Sam? >> Yeah. Uh you guys poured it on late, but um so maybe the stats don't play it out, but in that moment, how big was was Blake's almost intercept almost pick six there? >> No, I mean turnovers are a huge part of the game. You know, you felt that momentum a little bit starting to slide. um you know, you didn't get off the field, you know, when you when you needed to earlier and had a penalty and to come back and change the game, you know, not only from a field position standpoint, but really momentum. Um and I think that was kind of the dagger. So, I thought I thought it was a huge play in the game and the momentum of the game. So, uh he's another guy that's had a really good year and a great dude. So, I was really happy for him. >> U Pete, obviously this time last year, you had a million things on your plate and then over the few days after the Egg Bowl. this year. You've got a little while before the the bowl comes. The decisions that you're going to make, are they mostly made or are these decisions that you've got to sit down and think about over the next few days? >> No, I mean, I think, you know, everything's still in the evaluation phase of everything. You know, I made it a point. It's it's our responsibility to get through this season and finish it the right way, the best that we can. Um, and so now, you know, we're through that regular season. You know, the next thing for us is we got signing day on Wednesday. You know, we got to finish this thing really strong. Uh, I think we got a really good class right now. We still got a couple targets out there. Uh, so these next couple days are going to be focused on nothing but, you know, keeping that class intact and then, you know, potentially adding a couple guys to it. Uh, and that takes the whole building. A lot of these guys in the building have developed those relationships over the last couple years. So, that's all of our responsibility. That's our job uh to finish this class the right way. Uh, so then I think you get through that and then it's a discretionary week for us in the wait room. Uh, and then we'll really re-evaluate everything from a player coaching perspective moving forward. Uh, what do we need to do to give us our best chance to compete at championship level? >> Pete, what have you learned most about being a head coach for the first time? >> Uh, that you don't have it all figured out. That's for damn sure. No. Um, you know, I mean, I think it's a lot like life, man. I don't think anything goes exactly how you planned it, you know, and you've got all these plans and I'm I'm big setting everything up and I don't like the gray. I like everything black and white and I like everybody understanding here's my drive description, here's my expectation of it and all those type of things. Uh, and adversity is going to hit, you know, in every area of your life. And so, uh, I think some of those things this year, I think when we look back and really evaluate it, uh, I think some injuries occurred, the ball didn't always bounce our way. And then there's some things that I could have done better that we could have done better. Um there's times to where we could have played a lot better. Uh we could have done our job as players, too. So, you know, normally to me when you look back at it all, it's not normally just one thing, you know, and I think, uh it's my responsibility to make sure that we go run the course of this season like we did and then step back and not make an emotional decision, you know, and really look at the information and make sure we're making the best decision moving forward. Uh and that's what I'm going to do. within the will >> as far as the player piece. Uh Pete, what do the next couple weeks look like for everybody else? You know, you heard about Will and the considerations, but uh in terms of meetings or whatever it might be between like what does the next couple weeks look like in that? >> Yeah, you know, for us a lot a lot of that will be dictated off of the what you know, what bowl game we end up in. But you know, this first week u is discretionary week in the weight room. Uh so we'll give them off from ball. Uh they'll get three workouts in, focus on school. Uh then the next week is is finals week, you know, so they got to finish really strong academically in the classroom. That's really important. We'll do a OTAA model in finals week. Uh that'll be player run that I think is really important uh to develop some leadership. And we'll start a leadership development program next week that I think will be really important moving forward. Um and then from there, you know, you kind of structure it to where that first week of bowl prep's not about the team, it's about us. And it's very camp-like and you go back to the fundamentals uh and really work on a lot of the young guys. uh and to really see where they're at and what's that going to look like moving forward. And then to us, we've always done a two-eek game model for the bowl game and you do a mock game week of the game plan and get after it and then come back and clean it up with a normal game week uh and kind of pull the load back a little bit so we can be fresh cuz obviously Christmas is involved, you know, so we'll give them a couple days off for Christmas, but um they'll get this week, you know, away from ball. We'll come back do OTAA model and weights and then we'll we'll get into it. go up top. >> Yeah, Pete, uh, four straight wins in the Egg Bowl for the first time since the mid1 1980s, I believe. What does it say about the state of the program that you guys have been able to have this much success against your instate rivals? >> Well, I think that it was built the right way, you know, and I didn't have anything to do with that. I think, you know, any elite program starts with leadership and I think, you know, that starts with Glenn up top and then from Keith, I think Keith's done an unbelievable job. Um, and then when you start winning, um, obviously becomes a national brand. I don't care what type of coach you are, if you don't have good players, it ain't going to matter. Um, so I think stacking a couple really elite years on top of each other, uh, has become sexy across the country and a place to come play. Um, I also think, you know, the people in this place and how they make them feel when they're here is very unique. And so I think that's gotten out and I think we've been able to get more guys on visits and get them here and when they get here, they really love it here. Um, so, uh, that that's to me, you know, we talked about this before when I first took the job of thinking like, all right, let's get to 10 a year and there's going to be statues of people around here, you know, and it's that second year it's like, all right, this is natty or bust. This feels like Tuscaloosa again. And that's what you want, right? And because everything's been invested, you got the right type of leadership, you got the right type of support. Um, and there's high expectations with that as there should be. And so, uh, I love feeling disappointed at being eight and four, you know, and being two on one possession games versus top 10 teams, you know, and never being the favorite in it and being pissed off. That's how it should be. And so, uh, we got to do a better job moving forward, but I think it's it's in the right it's head in the right direction. That's for sure. >> All right. More questions down below. >> All right. Thanks, guys. I appreciate it.
